candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis requires three components: Pott's puffy tumor (subperiosteal abscess/osteitis of the frontal bone), sinocutaneous fistula (the pus-discharging eyelid node as the fistulous tract), and chronic sinusitis as the underlying etiology. C001 captures only the chronic sinusitis component and misattributes the pathology to orbital involvement, whereas MRI/CT showed no orbital or intracranial abnormality — the lesion is a sinocutaneous fistula from the frontal sinus to the eyelid skin. The hallmark Pott's puffy tumor designation and fistula are absent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies chronic frontal sinusitis but omits Pott's puffy tumor (frontal bone osteitis/subperiosteal abscess) and sinocutaneous fistula, and incorrectly asserts orbital involvement not supported by imaging

case_quality_flags: Atypical Pott's puffy tumor presentation without classic frontal bone destruction on CT — expansion without osteolysis noted, which is unusual but reported in chronic low-grade cases
Sinocutaneous fistula to eyelid is a rare complication; absence of fever/headache and 2-year indolent course consistent with chronic rather than acute presentation
